- Peak concurrent clinicians (interactive queries during peak): ~18–24 (we expect highest load around 1–3pm PT, internal Pacific locations).
- Average request size: 220 tokens input, ~420 tokens output (we produce substantial summaries and suggested care plans). Peak batch of bulk summarizations later in the evening but those can be scheduled as background jobs.
- Data residency: US-only for now; we will need KMS integration and audit logs for all request payloads.
- Compliance: HITRUST in process, SOC2 already in place. Audit evidence bundle is required for our InfoSec team (will share the checklist).
- Procurement timeline: target PO by May 15; pilot (60-day) to start June 15.

Subject: Re: NobleCare hosting lanes & sizing — Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs

Team — reviewed the forecast and sketched two lane options below. I kept the math explicit so sales/procurement can pick the right tradeoff. Assumptions:
- Model: Redwood-Gen-70B q4f16 (production-optimized quantized variant) for parity with clinical-quality outputs. We also include an alternative combo using Redwood-Compact-13B for fast short responses + 70B for long summaries.
- Average generation per interactive request: 420 tokens output + 220 input = 640 tokens
- Effective gen throughput (70B q4f16) per H100 GPU: ~200 tokens/sec (single-stream, conservative for guarded production with KV caching benefits).
- Effective gen throughput (13B q4f16) per A100/L40: ~700 tokens/sec (for short responses).
- Target peak concurrent interactive sessions: 24 active at peak. SLO: p95 latency target <= 1.5s for interactive responses.

Calculation (70B-only lane):
- Per-request average latency = tokens / throughput = 640 / 200 = 3.2s (generation time) — so single-GPU per-request latency exceeds our 1.5s SLO. To meet p95 <= 1.5s we must design for parallelism: we target a system concurrency such that per-request service latency is bounded by batching and short-path fast-lane. Practically, that means using multiple GPUs to serve concurrent requests rather than relying on one GPU to sequentially serve many.
- Throughput required to achieve 1.5s avg response for 24 concurrent users: each active request must be served in ~1.5s => system needs 24 * (640/1.5) tokens/sec ≈ 24 * 427 = 10,248 tokens/sec total. At 200 tokens/sec per H100 -> ~52 H100 GPUs. That's a large footprint and likely not cost-effective. However, two mitigations apply: (1) KV/prefix caching for common templates reduces effective generation work by ~30% for clinical templates, (2) mixing in smaller model for short-turn interactions reduces pressure.

Recommended practical lane designs:
A) Dedicated mixed-lane (Recommended for predictable throughput + lower infra ops):
- Node mix: 6 x H100 (for heavy summarization tasks / long generations) + 8 x A100/L40 (for short responses & reranks) — total 14 GPUs.
- How it meets load: route short interactive queries (~70% of requests) to the 13B fleet (A100/L40) achieving p95 < 800ms; long summarizations and document-level generations to H100 nodes with intelligent routing and priority queuing (expected p95 ~1.6–2.0s for heavy generations during peak, but median lower).
- Autoscaling/burst: enable burst capacity to add 4 H100s from dedicated buffer during scheduled peak windows (billing at higher rate).
- Estimated committed monthly cost (infra + Redwood Dedicated fee): ~$92k/month (model compute + reserved capacity amortized).

B) Private (VPC / customer-managed) conservative lane (Recommended if NobleCare insists on full private tenancy and custom KMS/HSM):
- Node mix (on-prem or VPC-attached GPU hosts): 10 x H100 equivalent + 12 x A100/L40 equivalent — total 22 GPUs (extra capacity needed due to less aggressive multi-tenant pooling and slightly higher headroom requirements for reliability).
- Additional itemized work: KMS/HSM integration, private control plane install, network egress and routing validation, backup and audit log ingestion config. Lead time: 8–12 weeks for VPC, 12–16 weeks for on-prem.
- Estimated one-time onboarding & integration professional services: $85k–120k. Ongoing monthly run-rate (ops + infra amortized): ~$135k/month (higher than Dedicated due to smaller pooling efficiency).

C) Cost-conscious pilot lane (short-term for June pilot):
- Small dedicated trial: 3 x H100 + 4 x A100 for 60-day pilot with burst credits. Route only a subset of clinicians (approx. 6–8) to live interactive lane while bulk jobs run off-hours on cheaper spot capacity.
- Estimated 60-day pilot cost (reserved + burst): ~$38k (discounted trial pricing included).

Compliance notes (private vs dedicated):
- Dedicated: Redwood provides per-tenant encryption at rest, configurable KMS integration, and audit logs. For HITRUST evidence, we can provide an evidence bundle but configuration validation and SOC attestation mapping will be a joint activity; lead time ~3 weeks for paperwork.
- Private: gives NobleCare greater control over KMS and network isolation; we need a connectivity window for install and on-prem access for PS engineers. Expect extra evidence artifacts from customer infra team.

Action items for SOW & procurement:
1) Sales: pick lane A or B for SOW baseline (Marissa / Priyom). If customer wants cost predictability choose A with a reserved commit; if they require full tenancy choose B.
2) PS: prepare a 30–45 day implementation plan for Dedicated lane (with burst) and separate 12–16 week plan for Private.
3) Security: provide NobleCare with a checklist (we have a redwood_private_deploy_checklist.pdf) and SOC2/HITRUST mapping doc.

I attached a short capacity_pricing_options_v3.xlsx with per-GPU monthly run rates and a sample SOW line item list. Happy to walk through numbers with customer tomorrow morning.

—Evelyn
